title: Magnons in Metallic Altermagnetic $\text{KV}_2\text{Se}_2\text{O}$
authors: Daniel Lourenço R. Santos, António T. Costa
abstract: We investigate the spin excitation in altermagnetic vanadium oxyselenides, focusing on the metallic quasi-two-dimensional compound $\text{KV}_2\text{Se}_2\text{O}$. Using a fermionic Hamiltonian derived from ab initio calculations, we compute the transverse spin susceptibilities within the random phase approximation and extract the magnon dispersion relation. We show that the altermagnetic symmetry leads to characteristic degeneracies and directional splittings in both the electronic bands and the magnon spectra along high-symmetry paths of the Brillouin zone. The metallic $\text{KV}_2\text{Se}_2\text{O}$ exhibits finite magnon linewidths arising from the coupling to the particle-hole continuum. Furthermore, by fixing the magnitude of the wave vector and varying its in-plane direction, we uncover a pronounced angular dependence of the magnon energies and lifetimes, with complementary damping behavior between the two magnon branches. Upon including spin-orbit coupling, the system exhibits an out-of-plane easy c-axis anisotropy, which opens a magnon gap of approximately 6 meV at the $Γ$-point, possibly rendering the magnetic order stable at room temperature. Our results demonstrate that altermagnetism controls not only the dispersion but also the anisotropic decay of spin excitations, highlighting altermagnetic metals as promising platforms for directionally selective magnon transport.
summary: This theoretical study investigates magnon excitations in the altermagnetic metal $	ext{KV}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$ using RPA calculations on a derived tight-binding Hamiltonian. The authors demonstrate that altermagnetism dictates both the magnon dispersion and its anisotropic decay, while SOC opens a significant gap, making the material promising for spintronic applications.
main_problem: The study investigates spin excitations (magnons) in the metallic altermagnetic compound $	ext{KV}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$, focusing on how altermagnetic symmetry and spin-orbit coupling control the magnon dispersion and decay.
main_result: The calculations reveal characteristic degeneracies and directional splittings in the magnon spectra, and the inclusion of SOC opens a sizable anisotropy gap ($\approx 6 	ext{ meV}$) at the $\Gamma$-point, suggesting potential room-temperature magnetic stability.
method: The research employs a fermionic Hamiltonian derived from *ab initio* calculations, computing transverse spin susceptibilities within the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) to determine the magnon dispersion and linewidths.
model_or_system: The system is the metallic, quasi-two-dimensional altermagnetic vanadium oxyselenide, $	ext{KV}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$. The model uses a multi-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating both hopping terms and spin-orbit coupling ($H = H_0 + H_{	ext{SOC}}$).
key_observables: Magnon dispersion relation, magnon linewidths/lifetimes, angular dependence of magnon energies, and the $\Gamma$-point anisotropy gap ($\approx 6 	ext{ meV}$).
important_parameters: SOC parameters ($\lambda_V = 22 	ext{ meV}$, $\lambda_{	ext{Se}} = 206 	ext{ meV}$), and the characteristic energy scales in the GHz-to-THz range.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the C-type magnetic configuration and that the low-energy electronic states are well-described by the tight-binding model derived from DFT.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spin-resolved electronic bands showing altermagnetic splitting, magnon dispersion along high-symmetry paths (M–$\Gamma$-X–Y–$\Gamma$), and spectral density maps highlighting anisotropic damping.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the electronic structure via DFT/PAW to constructing an effective tight-binding Hamiltonian. It then applies RPA to calculate the magnon spectrum, analyzing the effects of altermagnetism, SOC, and finite lifetime broadening.
why_interesting: The detailed study of magnon damping due to coupling to the particle-hole continuum, combined with the prediction of directionally selective transport, provides a rich platform for understanding spin dynamics in correlated magnetic materials.
